arxiv-2012-15270.title: Signatures of bath-induced quantum avalanches in a many-body–localized system
arxiv-2012-15270.creator: Julian Léonard 1,∗,†, Sooshin Kim 1,†, Matthew Rispoli 1, Alexander Lukin 1, Robert Schittko 1, Joyce Kwan 1, Eugene Demler 2, Dries Sels 3,4, Markus Greiner 1,‡
arxiv-2012-15270.description: Abstract Strongly correlated systems can exhibit surprising phenomena when brought in a state far from equilibrium. A spectacular example are quantum avalanches, that have been predicted to run through a many-body–localized system and delocalize it. Quantum avalanches occur when the system is locally coupled to a small thermal inclusion that acts as a bath.

arxiv-2510-00688.title: Non-singular Bouncing Cosmology in f ⁡ ( R , G , T ) f(R,G,T) –Quintom model
arxiv-2510-00688.creator: Farzad Milani
arxiv-2510-00688.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Farzad Milani. We present a unified framework for non-singular bouncing cosmologies in modified gravity, combining f ⁡ ( R , G , T ) f(R,G,T) geometry with quintom scalar dynamics in a flat FLRW universe. While single-field models achieve phantom divide line (PDL) crossing and stable bounces, our f ⁡ ( R , G , T ) f(R,G,T) -quintom coupling provides a novel implementation of a double PDL crossing of ω eff \omega_{\text{eff}} during the bounce.

arxiv-2511-20584.title: A Tale of Two Geometries: Adaptive Optimizers and Non-Euclidean Descent
arxiv-2511-20584.creator: Shuo Xie, Tianhao Wang, Beining Wu, Zhiyuan Li
arxiv-2511-20584.description: Abstract Adaptive optimizers can reduce to normalized steepest descent (NSD) when only adapting to the current gradient, suggesting a close connection between the two algorithmic families. A key distinction between their analyses, however, lies in the geometries, e.g., smoothness notions, they rely on.

britannica-1911-colchicum.description: Article 'Colchicum' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 6), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. a perennial plant of the natural order, Liliaceae, found wild in rich moist meadow-land in England and Ireland, in middle and southern Europe, and in the Swiss Alps. pmc-13556717.title: 534. Striatal dopamine synthesis trajectory in first-episode psychosis during amisulpride monotherapy and after switch to aripiprazole: a one-year [18F]DOPA PET study
pmc-13556717.creator: S Kim, J Schubert, M Veronese, F Turkheimer, B C Lee, Y S Song, O Howes, E Kim
pmc-13556717.description: BackgroundSchizophrenia and related psychotic disorders are associated with elevated striatal dopamine synthesis from the first episode. While antipsychotics primarily improve symptoms through dopamine D₂ receptor blockade, it remains unclear whether they affect presynaptic dopamine synthesis due to mixed findings in prior studies. Amisulpride’s D₂/D₃ selectivity makes it ideal for studying dopaminergic changes in FEP under controlled conditions.

pmc-13606227.title: pH-/Temperature-Triggered Gel Transition of Hyperbranched PEI-g-PDMAEMA as a Dual-Responsive Inhibitor for Clay Hydration Control
pmc-13606227.creator: Ming Zhong, Yang Xiong
pmc-13606227.description: To mitigate clay hydration and wellbore instability during deepwater drilling, a pH/temperature dual-responsive graft copolymer, hyperbranched polyethylenimine-g-poly(2-(dimethylamino)ethyl methacrylate) (HPEI-g-PDMAEMA), was designed and synthesized via free radical polymerization. Optimized synthesis at an HPEI/DMAEMA mass ratio of 1:2 with 2.4% AIBN at 70 °C for 10 h yielded a grafting ratio of 35.2% and a molecular weight of 84.3 kDa.
